 Tottenham v Crystal Palace (17:30 GMT) 
 The teams are out and this relentless day of football continues. 
 27 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Martinez is a liability' published at 17:25 GMT 17:25 GMT 
 FT: Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United 
 Danny Murphy 
Former Liverpool midfielder on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 Got to be of a positive mindset, and you have got to keep going.
 That first half was really good, they set up well, they made chances and looked like a team again. Lisandro Martinez has got a lot to answer too, because the first goal was mainly his fault. The sending off is absolutely ridiculous.
 Obviously, he is going to apologise in the dressing room, but his mindset is not right to play. You can't rely on him. He is a liability.
 58 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Not good enough' published at 17:24 GMT 17:24 GMT 
 FT: Man City 0-1 Brighton 
 Manchester City 
 Manchester City midfielder Elliot Anderson speaking to Sky Sports: 
 "We created a lot of chances. Disappointing to lose. Didn't manage to put chances away, on another day we put three or four away, We have to bounce back for the Champions League game in a couple of days.
 "Three in midfield, man for man and we had the wingers staying high and wide. We did have the width but we didn't manage to get the chances away which is unfortunate but we'll have to work on it.
 "We're all disappointed. Not good enough, we don't want to be losing games but we've got to stick together. We've had a great start to the season, two disappointing results now but we have to stick together."
 Anything in multiple handball claims? "I thought so on the pitch but I haven't seen them back."
 10 21 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 17:23 GMT 17:23 GMT 
 Tottenham v Crystal Palace (17:30 GMT) 
 Spurs are a sucker for a lightshow and they're having one right now. 
 Either that or the lights are a bit faulty. 
 24 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'It's always easier when you won' published at 17:21 GMT 17:21 GMT 
 Tottenham v Crystal Palace (17:30 GMT) 
 Crystal Palace 
 Image source, Getty Images Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage speaking to Sky Sports about Dean Henderson's return: "He is really important for us. That's why he is our captain."
 On carrying momentum from the midweek Carabao Cup win: "It's always easier when you won and when you work after a win. It was really important for us to quality on Wednesday.
 On Tottenham: "They like to play with the ball, the ball moves quickly too that's why we have to be aware of what can happen on the pitch and closing the spaces. When we recover the ball we have to do the best decision."
 11 5 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 17:19 GMT 17:19 GMT 
 Tottenham v Crystal Palace (17:30 GMT) 
 What are we all expecting here then?
 Will Spurs make it three wins on the spin or will Palace relieve the pressure on boss Pierre Sage?
 35 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'When Maddison feels good, he plays' published at 17:17 GMT 17:17 GMT 
 Tottenham v Crystal Palace (17:30 GMT) 
 Tottenham Hotspur 
 Tottenham boss Roberto de Zerbi speaking to Sky Sports about James Maddison's absence: "Just for the physical condition, to be clear James is very important for us. When he feels good, he plays."
 On Solanke and Marmoush: "The most important is the space they find during the game. Marmoush is a 10, I think they can play together. Marmoush has played many times with another striker, no problem."
 On the importance of building momentum: "To keep the focus on the ball, the right spirit, mentality and union with the players. 15 days ago we were last in the table and we can't forget it. Crystal Palace are a good team.
 "He has a clear style, clear idea. It is a tough game for us for sure but also for them."
 43 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Palace proving too easy to breach published at 17:15 GMT 17:15 GMT 
 Tottenham v Crystal Palace (17:30 GMT) 
 Tottenham away used to be a trip of trepidation across London for Crystal Palace fans but the tide has certainly turned in recent years.
 After nine straight top-flight losses at Spurs they have won on their last two visits, with their 3-1 victory in March particularly impressive.
 However, this is a Palace team in a very different spot. Defeat to Newcastle on Sunday was their fifth in just eight league matches under new boss Pierre Sage.
 They sit 17th having conceded a top-flight high of 19 goals in eight matches, the second most they have let in at this stage of a top-flight season after 22 in 1980-81.
 Of the 24 previous Premier League teams to concede 19 after eight games, 14 went on to be relegated. And another concerning stat is that they have let in at least two goals in 12 of their last 14 top-flight games.
 These defensive frailties, though, can't all be put at Sage's feet as they predate the Frenchman's summer arrival. Their tally of conceding 50 goals in 2026 is not only a Premier League high, but it's also six more than they conceded in the whole of 2025 and they still have 10 league matches to play this year.
 20 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Martinez is not the answer' published at 17:13 GMT 17:13 GMT 
 FT: Chelsea 2-0 Manchester United 
 Danny Murphy 
Former Liverpool midfielder on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 On whether he would play Lisandro Martinez again...
 No, I wouldn't, only because he looks like he has already gone. 
 His head isn't right. He is not going to be there long term, that is evident.
 You have to put the club first. Michael has got to make some big decisions. You can't have a liability in your team.
 People talked about Romero for years, and it is turning into that a little bit. That petulance, that behaviour on the pitch is not acceptable.
 He has been poor for a while and he has had injury problems. He is not the answer. 
 111 6 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Amount of bodies on the line today was incredible' published at 17:12 GMT 17:12 GMT 
 FT: Man City 0-1 Brighton 
 Brighton & Hove Albion 
 Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen speaking to Sky Sports: "Unbelievable feeling. We go 1-0 up and then to hang tight the last 30-40 minutes we completely lost control of the game. The manager said this morning we have to dig deep and that's what we did. So happy to get over the line and can't wait to celebrate with the boys."
 On if Brighton are in the title race: "We are on game nine so not really. We'll take it game by game. See what happens because we have loads of games. Just focussing every day on what's ahead of us and the job we have. We will continue to do that and see where it leaves us at the end of the season. We are happy with the way we are playing - not just the results but the way we are playing too. We have to continue to develop that style and ruthlessness and we can do great things."
 On keeping a clean sheet: "Hard to point out one thing, the mentality to keep the ball out of the net - how hard we work. The amount of bodies put on the line today is incredible and credit to all the boys and staff and how hard we worked to keep the clean sheets. Hopefully we can get many more."
 On if this was one of his best personal performances: "I don't know - it was a good game from all of us. Happy to help the team and make some important saves but I wasn't the only one. I think there were four or five shots blocked in an amazing way as well. Joint effort from everyone. We celebrate and go again."
 116 2 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Maddison relief for Spurs published at 17:08 GMT 17:08 GMT 
 Tottenham v Crystal Palace (17:30 GMT) 
 Phil McNulty 
BBC Sport chief football writer at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium 
 It will be something of a disappointment for Spurs fans that James Maddison is only on the bench after his sparkling return from injury, but there will also be a tinge of relief because there were fears he might face another lengthy lay-off when he went down injured during the win at Chelsea last Saturday.
 Head coach Roberto De Zerbi offered assurances that his groin problem was not serious, and so it has proved as he is named on the bench for the home game against Crystal Palace.
 Image source, Getty Images 
 66 15 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 get involved Get Involved published at 17:06 GMT 17:06 GMT 
 Click 'Get Involved' on this page to have your say 
 A lot of pundits have predicted a title race between Arsenal and Man City but with Brighton beating both title contenders, when do we begin to take Brighton seriously as title contenders?
 Sam, Newport 
 Seagulls stealing chips in Manchester!
 Andy, France 
 This league is interesting. No one is sure what team will beat the other team. Brighton beating City at the Etihad shows why the Premier League is top and full of drama.
 Lanre, Lagos 
 483 39 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 17:05 GMT 17:05 GMT 
 FT: Man City 0-1 Brighton 
 Manchester City have attempted 21 shots in this game, their highest total in a single match in the Premier League this season.
 Erling Haaland had four shots but it didn't feel like it. The Norwegian struggled this afternoon.
 Image source, Getty Images 
 211 9 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'I was waiting for this goal for so long' published at 17:03 GMT 17:03 GMT 
 FT: Brentford 2-0 Nottm Forest 
 Brentford 
 Brentford goalscorer Igor Thiago speaking to Premier League Productions : "I'm really happy today. The change is there today. We fight, we did what Keith [Andrews] told us to do and we got the three points.
 On the physicality of the game: "I really enjoy it, I like it this kind of game - it suits me really well."
 On what his goal means: "It means a lot to me. I was waiting for this goal for so long this season. Thank you Lord, to score one more goal at home. I am really happy."
